column1: # huc6280-opcodes.tsv: the HuC6280 opcode table, transcribed from the manufacturer manual page images (plan 03-08; D-96, D-97; ER-1, ER-9; R-1, R-2).

# This file is numeric data with page cites. It holds no manual text and no page image (ER-9). It is the independent second table that plan 03-09 compares the core table with, and the matrix input of scripts/xasm-check (D-129).
# It was made before src/core/cpu_ops.def existed, and no value in it was taken from a DuoSpool source, from ca65 output or from another emulator.
# Method: the opcode map H8-25 (hardware manual page 25, PDF page 28) was read as a page image, cell by cell (mnemonic, mode label, bytes, cycles).

# Every instruction page S8-17 to S8-108 (software manual, PDF page n+2, footer checked) was read as a page image for its machine code, mode, bytes and cycles. The flags come from Tables 2-3-1 to 2-3-3 (S8-7, S8-8, S8-9), read as page images, not from the OCR layer.

# Verifier: gsd-executor (Claude Sonnet 5.5) reading page images rendered at 110 to 300 dpi. Date: 2026-11-11. The PDFs are the three of 03-RESEARCH, fetched to a scratch directory outside the repository, sha256 equal to the recorded values (fixtures/lib/TOOLS.md).

# Result of the two reads: the 232 opcodes that have an instruction page agree between the map and the pages in mnemonic, mode, bytes and cycles, except the printing errors listed below (CSL and CSH appear only in the map). Where the two differ the machine code printed on the instruction page decides.
# Columns, one row per opcode 00 to FF in order, TAB separated: opcode (two hex digits), mnemonic, mode, bytes, cycles, flags, cite. The column header is not a data row, so it is not repeated here.
# Mnemonics: BBRn, BBSn, RMBn and SMBn carry their bit number (the manual writes BBRi, TAMi and the like); TAM and TMA are the TAMi and TMAi of the manual; the manual's NCP in the map is NOP.

# Modes: IMPLIED, ACC (accumulator, written A), IMM, ZP, ZPX, ZPY, ABS, ABSX, ABSY, IND (zero page indirect), INDX, INDY, ABSIND (JMP (hhll)), ABSINDX (JMP (hhll,X)), REL, ZPREL (BBR and BBS: zero page byte then relative byte),

# BLK (block transfer: source, destination and length words), MASK (TAM and TMA: one operand byte, a single set bit, 2 to the power i; the manual labels them IMPLIED), IMMZP, IMMZPX, IMMABS, IMMABSX (TST: immediate byte first, then the address), and - for an undefined opcode.

# Bytes: instruction length. Cycles: the base count printed by the manual, nothing added: the taken-branch, T-flag and decimal adders live in their own ledger rows (LED-CPU-0002). Block transfers print * in the map; the formula is 17+6x with x the length (H8-6, S8-89), written 17+6x here.

# The map footnote of H8-25 prints that formula as 17+16z, a misprint (R-1); it is not used. TII, TIN, TIA, TAI and TDD tables are on S8-98, S8-100, S8-96, S8-89 and S8-94; the flowchart pages S8-88, S8-93, S8-95 and S8-97 were seen and S8-99 was not read.

# Flags: eight characters in the order N V T B D I Z C as the manual tables show them. A letter means the flag is set from the result, - means unaffected, 0 or 1 means set to that value. In the N position 7 means memory bit 7 and in the V position 6 means memory bit 6 (BIT, TRB, TSB, TST).
# RESTORED (PLP, RTI) means the flags are loaded from the stack. unlisted (CSL, CSH) means no flag-table row and no instruction page exists for the opcode: the map shows it, the flag table does not.

# UNDEF: the 22 empty cells of the H8-25 map. Their bytes, cycles and flags are - because the empty cells give no numbers, and scripts/xasm-check skips them. The complement of the 234 defined rows is exactly these 22 opcodes.
# Cite: H8-25 plus the instruction page, plus the flag table page, plus H8-6 for block transfers. CSL and CSH have only H8-25 (the software manual has no page for them, research mismatch 4).
# Printing errors of the manual read as the intended value (research mismatch 7 and the new ones found here):

#   H8-25 grid, opcodes 34 to 37: the printed cells read, in order of opcode, AND ZP,X 2/4, RMB3 ZP 2/7, ROL (IND) 2/7 and ROL ZP,X 2/6. S8-25, S8-18, S8-68 and S8-67 give 34 BIT ZP,X 2/4, 35 AND ZP,X 2/4, 36 ROL ZP,X 2/6 and 37 RMB3 ZP 2/7. This file follows the instruction pages.
#   H8-25 grid, opcodes B4 and B5: the printed cells read LDA ZP,X 2/4 and LDA ZP 2/7. S8-55 and S8-53 give B4 LDY ZP,X 2/4 and B5 LDA ZP,X 2/4. This file follows the instruction pages.

#   H8-25 grid: opcode 7D prints its mode as (ABS,X) where S8-17 gives ABS,X; the letter O stands for the digit 0 in RMB0, BBR0, ST0, SMB0 and BBS0; 6D prints ADS for ADC, 40 prints RT1 for RTI, 43 prints TRAi for TMAi, EA prints NCP for NOP, 88 prints DY for DEY.
#   Instruction pages: S8-74 prints BSC for SBC at F1, S8-47 prints AND for EOR at 5D, S8-96 prints TAI for TIA at E3. The mode word IMPLID printed on many pages is IMPLIED.

#   The reference-page column of Tables 2-3-1 to 2-3-3 lists several pages that differ from the instruction pages found by footer (for example SET at S8-88 where the page is S8-78). The cites here use the footer page number of the page that was read.
# Whether the manual itself is right about the hardware is not claimed: this file says what the page images print (documentary, E1 only after the re-read that ER-1 and R-8 require for any promotion).
